security_audit.summary: All 96 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown syntax, benign local cache writes, molecule-validation language, and passive documentation links. However, two examples use pickle.load without authenticity checks, creating a high-severity code-execution risk if a cache file is replaced or untrusted.

remediation.issue: The embedding cache examples deserialize pickle files without verifying their source or integrity.
remediation.suggestion: Use a non-executable array format such as NumPy NPZ, or verify a trusted cache with strict ownership, permissions, and integrity checks before loading.

content.user_title: Build Molecular ML Features with Molfeat
content.value_statement: Molecular datasets need consistent numerical representations before modeling. This skill guides Molfeat selection, configuration, featurization, caching, and integration with common machine-learning workflows.
actual_capabilities: Selects fingerprints, descriptors, pretrained transformers, and graph models for specific molecular learning tasks.
Shows how to transform SMILES strings or RDKit molecules into numerical feature arrays.
Configures batch processing, parallel execution, invalid-molecule handling, and reusable transformer state.
Integrates Molfeat with scikit-learn workflows for QSAR, virtual screening, and similarity search.
Explains ModelStore discovery, model comparison, combined features, and chunked processing.
Provides examples for saving configurations and caching expensive pretrained embeddings.
limitations: The skill provides guidance and examples; it does not include Molfeat, RDKit, datasets, or trained prediction models.
Optional featurizers require extra packages, model downloads, memory, and sometimes substantial compute.
Example results require scientific validation and do not establish predictive accuracy or chemical suitability.
Pickle cache examples are unsafe for files from untrusted or writable locations.

use_cases.title: Prepare QSAR Features
use_cases.description: Choose reproducible fingerprints or descriptors and connect them to a scikit-learn property prediction pipeline.

use_cases.title: Screen Compound Libraries
use_cases.description: Batch-featurize candidate molecules, score them with a classifier, and rank likely active compounds.

use_cases.title: Prototype Molecular Embeddings
use_cases.description: Compare ChemBERTa, graph models, and classical fingerprints before committing to an architecture.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Featurizer
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend a Molfeat featurizer for [task] using [dataset size] molecules and [model type]. Explain accuracy, speed, dependencies, and feature dimensions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner selection for a new molecular machine-learning task

prompt_templates.title: Create a Featurization Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Molfeat workflow for SMILES data in [input format]. Include validation, error handling, batching, parallel settings, and reproducible configuration.
prompt_templates.scenario: Building a reliable dataset preparation process

prompt_templates.title: Compare Molecular Representations
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [featurizer A], [featurizer B], and [featurizer C] for [prediction task]. Define a fair evaluation plan and resource estimates.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Production Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a production Molfeat pipeline for [volume] molecules. Cover chunking, trusted caching, configuration versioning, monitoring, failure handling, and deployment constraints.

output_examples.input: Which featurizer should I try first for a small QSAR regression dataset?
output: Start with ECFP at radius 2 or 3 and 2,048 bits as a strong, efficient baseline.
Compare it with RDKit 2D descriptors when interpretability matters.
Use scaffold-aware validation and save the exact featurizer configuration.

output_examples.input: How should I process one million SMILES without exhausting memory?
output: Validate inputs and process fixed-size chunks instead of creating one full feature matrix.
Write each completed chunk to a safe array format and record failed molecule indices.
Benchmark worker count because maximum parallelism can increase memory pressure.

output_examples.input: Should I use ChemBERTa or ECFP for an initial experiment?
output_examples.output: Use ECFP for the first baseline because it is fast and inexpensive. Add ChemBERTa when transfer learning may justify extra dependencies and compute.

best_practices: Validate SMILES, preserve row mappings, and report failed transformations before model training.
Save featurizer configuration, package versions, preprocessing rules, and random seeds with every experiment.
Benchmark simple fingerprints first, then add pretrained embeddings only when measured performance supports their cost.
anti_patterns: Do not compare featurizers with different data splits or inconsistent preprocessing.
Do not load pickle caches from shared, downloaded, or otherwise untrusted locations.
Do not use maximum parallelism without measuring memory consumption and throughput.

faq.question: What input formats does this skill cover?
faq.answer: The examples primarily use SMILES strings and RDKit molecule objects.

faq.question: Which featurizer is a practical starting point?
faq.answer: ECFP is a common fast baseline. Add 2D descriptors when interpretability is important.

faq.question: Does the skill install Molfeat automatically?
faq.answer: No. It documents installation commands, optional extras, and usage patterns.

faq.question: Can it use pretrained molecular models?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers ChemBERTa, ChemGPT, GIN, Graphormer, and other models available through Molfeat.

faq.question: How are invalid molecules handled?
faq.answer: Molfeat transformers can continue after failures and return missing results for invalid inputs. Preserve indexes when filtering those results.

faq.question: Is the documented pickle cache safe?
faq.answer: Only for files you fully trust. Prefer a non-executable format for shared or externally supplied caches.
